newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to redeem early its 2008 Aztec bonds at par.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to redeem early its 2008 Aztec bonds at par.

text.p: The Mexican government said on Tuesday it would redeem, at par, all of its outstanding $2.556 billion collateralised floating rate bonds due in 2008, commonly known as Aztec bonds, on March 27 this year.
"There are currently Aztec Bonds with a principal amount of $1.057 billion outstanding," the finance ministry said in a statement.
About $1.5 billion of the bonds had been cancelled in several operations between 1992 and 1996, leaving about $1.06 billion outstanding, it said.
"In accordance with the terms and conditions of the Aztec bonds, interest thereon shall accrue until but not excluding the redemption date," the ministry said.
The finance ministry said the early redemption of the Aztec bonds, issued in 1988, would be financed by medium-term debt issues this year at a lower cost.
Mexico would thus save about $80 million in costs and free up about $400 million in collateral associated with the Aztec bond issue, it said.
